reasoning: Both attempts fix the main freeze the same way: one instance per block, properties set before parenting, and a shared Heartbeat budget of 3 ms and 200 blocks per frame. B follows the load-reservation rule exactly, but its unload frees all cells and the slot at once and loops over all 20k parts in the leave frame. For about 1.7 s, anyone can place blocks that overlap the old parts. A spreads reservation over about 4 frames, but it never creates overlapping parts. It unloads incrementally, frees each cell only when its block is gone, and holds the slot until the plot is empty. That makes A the more robust fix, despite its extra complexity and a possible `next()` slowdown during unload.

criteria.note: `blockInfo[part] = { plot, ownerId, placedAt, cell }` replaces both value objects; placedAt is kept for saved blocks (`queuedPlacedAt`) and placed ones (`os.time()`).
Each block is cloned from a fully set-up, unparented template, then `part.CFrame` is set before `part.Parent = plot.folder`.

`onHeartbeat` caps work at FRAME_BUDGET 3 ms, MAX_CREATES_PER_FRAME 200 and MAX_DESTROYS_PER_FRAME 1000, and unloading is fully spread out. `next(plot.blocks)` after each delete may slow down as the table empties, but the time budget limits it.

Reservation runs over about 4 frames (`reserveSome`, up to 5000 per frame), so cells aren't all reserved before the first yield. Overlaps can't happen, because `createSome` waits until `plot.saved` is nil. Leaving mid-load releases queued cells and destroys built blocks, and the slot is held until unload finishes.
`info.ownerId ~= player.UserId` replaces the owner check and also rejects anything outside the plots; reach uses `info.cell`, the same position as before; placement validation is unchanged.
Says builds appear over about 1.7 s at 200 per frame and unload in about 1/3 s, describes the short reservation window and the wait for a slot, and has a 'Not verified' section.
